sections.h2: What the Clermont County recorder does
sections.html:
The recorder files deeds, mortgages and mortgage releases and keeps them as the permanent land record. Unlike a car title, a deed is not held by the office or the bank while a loan is outstanding. The original goes back to whoever submitted it, and the recorder keeps an imaged copy.

The office is at 101 East Main Street, Batavia, Ohio 45103, open weekdays from eight in the morning to four in the afternoon. The main line is 513-732-7236. A title company normally handles recording for both sides of a sale. A seller without one can still walk the deed through three counters in Batavia, and each checks something different: the tax map office checks the legal description, the auditor checks the fee and the transfer, and the recorder checks the format of the document.

Adding a spouse, removing a former owner or fixing a spelling takes a newly drafted deed, so see an attorney first. The office records what it is handed and does not draft.

You can e-file through an approved partner, mail the packet, or bring it in. E-filing is fastest: e-filed documents are typically recorded the same day and show online within 24 hours. Partner companies are listed on the recorder's e-filing page, and fees are paid by ACH.

  • E-file: submissions are processed from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. on business days. Anything arriving later is worked the next business day. Plats and DD214 discharge papers must come in on paper.
  • Mail: send the prepared document, a check payable to the Clermont County Treasurer, the auditor's conveyance forms, a cover letter naming a contact, and a return envelope with postage already on it. The office will not pay to send your document back.
  • In person: start at the Tax Map Office for a legal description stamp, go to the Auditor for the transfer stamp, and only then go to the recorder's counter.

Expect 1 to 14 days to finish recording, depending on how the packet arrives. Auditor fees need their own check, also made out to the county treasurer, when they travel with the deed.

The recorder's schedule prints a basic charge of $34.00 for the first two sides and $8.00 for each added side on 8 1/2 by 14 inch paper. Statewide base fees changed in October 2024 under Senate Bill 94, so call 513-732-7236 to confirm the figure before you write the check.

A short payment sends the paper back unrecorded. Card payments carry a 2.5% convenience charge with a $2.00 floor.

Transfers pass through the auditor first. The conveyance fee is $4.00 for each $1,000 of consideration, rounded up to the nearest hundred dollars, and the transfer fee is $0.50 for each parcel. Those standards were adopted under Revised Code 319.203 and took effect January 1, 2024.

Each deed travels with a state conveyance form: DTE 100 for a priced sale, or DTE 100EX where the seller claims the fee does not apply. A seller who held the Homestead reduction for the preceding or current tax year adds DTE 101, and a seller with farmland under current agricultural use valuation adds DTE 102. The auditor is at the same Batavia address and keeps weekday hours until 4:30 p.m., a half hour past the recorder's closing for new filings.

Four problems explain most returned deeds, and each can push a closing back by days.

  • The check is short, or it names the wrong payee.
  • The document has no legal description, or the image is too poor to read.
  • A Social Security number is printed anywhere on the instrument.
  • The deed arrives without the tax map and auditor stamps.

A paper that fails the margin and font rules in Revised Code 317.114 can still be recorded, but the $20 surcharge applies. The recorder holds plats of condominiums, subdivisions and city lots only. If the land is acreage with no lot number, the tax map survey sits with the County Engineer, and the auditor's property search shows the same surveys online.

sections.h2: Searching records and preventing deed fraud
sections.html:
Recorded documents from 1980 forward can be searched on the recorder's website. Printing from the computer at the counter costs 10 cents a page, and pulling a paper book costs $0.25 a page. A copy ordered by mail runs $2.00 a page plus a prepaid return envelope.

The recorder also runs FraudSleuth, a free account that sends an email alert when a document is recorded in a name you enter. Set up a separate profile for each spelling, such as first and last, or first, middle initial and last, with no commas or periods. An alert does not prove fraud, since another person may share the name, but it gives an owner a reason to phone 513-732-7236.

The recorder, the probate judge and the clerk of the common pleas court also promote a Good Deeds Program, aimed at helping owners lower or avoid probate court costs. An heir who inherited a Clermont County house should ask the recorder about it before listing.

Once a loan is retired, the lender sends a release, and the recorder cross-references it to the original mortgage. The clerk of courts, 513-732-7560, files foreclosure suits, and the sheriff, 513-732-7087, lists auctions.

The county has 91,743 housing units and 84,955 households, and about 89.3% of residents had not moved within the prior year. Median monthly owner costs run $1,677 with a mortgage and $646 without. Ask your lender how long it takes to send the release after a payoff, since the recorder indexes that paper only after it arrives.

Property tax belongs to the treasurer, whose line is 513-732-7254. The recorder will not accept tax payments and refers callers there.

sections.h2: Selling fast with a cash buyer
sections.html: A cash sale still needs the deed recorded, so the steps above stay the same. The title company usually gathers the stamps, the conveyance form and the checks, and e-filing lets the deed record the same day in most cases. Before you sign, make sure no Social Security number appears on the deed, confirm the payee name on each check, and ask the title agent whether a mortgage release is still waiting to be recorded.

faqs.q: Which office takes a Clermont County deed for recording?
faqs.a: The Clermont County Recorder, 101 East Main Street, Batavia, or an approved e-filing partner. In-person deeds first get stamps from the Tax Map Office and the Auditor.

faqs.q: How long does Clermont County take to record a deed?
faqs.a: The office quotes 1 to 14 days depending on the submission method. E-filed documents are typically recorded the same day and appear online within 24 hours.

faqs.q: What is the Clermont County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The auditor charges $4.00 per $1,000 of consideration, rounded up to the nearest hundred dollars, plus a transfer fee of $0.50 per parcel. These are paid to the auditor, separate from the recorder's check.

faqs.q: Can the recorder write or correct my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office records documents but does not prepare them. Adding or changing a name needs a new deed drawn up, so contact an attorney.

faqs.q: Does a Clermont County deed need a Homestead statement?
faqs.a: Yes, when the seller was entitled to the Homestead reduction for the preceding or current tax year. DTE 101 goes with the conveyance form.
